title: Fair housing - disability accommodations and modifications
facts: The Fair Housing Act can require housing providers to make reasonable accommodations in rules, policies, practices or services when necessary for a person with a disability to use and enjoy housing, unless a legal exception applies.
The Act also provides rights concerning reasonable modifications to premises, with responsibility for costs and restoration depending on the circumstances and housing program.

A housing provider may request information necessary to evaluate a disability-related request when the disability or need is not obvious, but federal fair-housing rules limit what can properly be demanded.
